---
title: "Would a veterinary agreement be a boost for UK-EU agri-food exports?"
description: "Drawing on 279 trade agreements worldwide, this piece finds a UK-EU veterinary deal built on mutual recognition could lift UK agri-food exports to the EU by 22.5% within a decade."
date: "2024-06-17"
categories: [brexit, agrifood]
---

Evidence from 279 trade agreements worldwide shows that comprehensive,
legally binding commitments on agricultural standards can substantially
expand agri-food trade — in the UK-EU case, potentially raising UK
agri-food exports to the EU by 22.5% over ten years. Crucially, the analysis
shows this doesn't require the UK to simply adopt EU rules wholesale: mutual
recognition of equivalent standards can deliver the gains. The politics of
getting there remain hard, but the piece argues a supplementary veterinary
agreement sitting alongside the existing TCA is economically well worth
pursuing.

**Originally published on UK in a Changing Europe**, June 17, 2024.
